post.caption: A Swiss coin banned a forelock. In 1895, Switzerland held a contest to design a new gold coin. 21 entries were judged, and none won first place. Medallist Fritz Landry came second and then revised his design. Critics said his Helvetia looked too young and romantic. Trial coins in 1896 showed a lock of hair on her forehead. Federal Councillor Walter Hauser called the forelock frivolous. In January 1897, Landry removed it, so only 12 forelock coins exist. Swiss people nicknamed the coin Vreneli, a pet form of Verena. Its edge carries 22 stars, one for each Swiss canton.
